assessment.rationale: Held: the project's deliverable, water harvested from air for villages without another source, is a known and deployed answer. SOURCE Global's solar hydropanels supply off-grid communities, for example 200 panels producing about 160 gallons a day on the Warm Springs Reservation, Oregon, an indigenous community in Palawan, Philippines (more than 40,000 litres a year) and rural and tribal Arizona programmes for over 3,000 people (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/ipd/project_profiles/or_warm_springs.aspx; https://www.rappler.com/technology/innovations/source-hydropanels-conservation-international-bintat-karis-palawan/). CloudFisher fog nets on Mount Boutmezguida supply about 18 litres a day each to roughly 1,000 villagers in Morocco through Dar Si Hmad (https://www.wipo.int/en/web/wipo-magazine/articles/pioneering-fog-harvesting-technology-helps-relieve-water-shortages-in-arid-regions-40409), and Yaghi's MOF harvester has been field-tested in the Mojave at 0.7 L per kg per day (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2019/08/190827170603.htm). Honest limit: the 200,000,000-person KPI is unmet because hydropanels yield only 2 to 5 L per panel per day at roughly US$0.12 to 0.30 per litre, fog nets need fog, and MOF output falls to about 0.2 L/kg/day at 7 percent humidity, with no village-scale MOF plant confirmed. Those are cost and arid-yield problems; harvesting air water for a village is a known answer, so under the 29 September 2026 rule the project is not opened as new work. A reframed project on low-cost sorbent harvesters for very low humidity would need its own prior-art basis.

additionalSearches.query: SOURCE Global hydropanels villages deployed liters per day cost atmospheric water
additionalSearches.finding: Hydropanels make about 2 to 5 L per panel per day off-grid; Warm Springs Reservation has 200 donated panels making 160 gallons a day; Palawan indigenous community over 40,000 L a year; Arizona programme for over 3,000 people. Costs about US$2,000 per panel plus installation or US$0.12 to 0.30 per litre; viable mainly for philanthropic programmes.

additionalSearches.query: fog collection CloudFisher Dar Si Hmad Morocco village water supply liters per day
additionalSearches.finding: CloudFisher on Mount Boutmezguida: about 36,000 to 37,400 L per foggy day from 1,600 square metres of mesh, supplying about 18 L per person per day to roughly 1,000 to 1,200 villagers; yields 1.6 to 22 L per square metre depending on site; water meets WHO standards. Works only where fog occurs.

additionalSearches.query: metal-organic framework water harvester desert low humidity liters per kg per day 2025 2026 village scale WaHa
additionalSearches.finding: Yaghi MOF harvester: 1.3 L per kg MOF per day (ACS Central Science 2019), 0.7 L/kg/day in Mojave field tests and 0.2 L/kg/day at 7 percent RH; Water Harvesting Inc. planned 7 to 10 L/day units; a 20,000 L/day village harvester was an aspirational 2019 projection with no confirmed deployment.

additionalSearches.query: "atmospheric water harvesting" AND (sorbent OR MOF) AND "field" 2024-2026 (Europe PMC)
additionalSearches.finding: Europe PMC returns 100 records 2024-2026, including Chemistries and materials for atmospheric water harvesting (Chem Soc Rev 2024) and sorption-based AWH progress (Sci Bull 2024); active materials research on yield and energy, consistent with the device class existing and cost-yield being the open gap.
